sentences.4.3 Skal vi møtes en dag?: 4.3 Shall we meet up one day?
sentences.Hei, Håvard! Lenge siden sist! Hvordan g: Hi, Håvard! Long time no see! How's it going?
sentences.Takk, det går bra! Og med deg?: Thanks, it's going well! And you?
sentences.Fint, men jeg har mye å gjøre. Jeg jobbe: Fine, but I have a lot to do. I work a lot, and I have the children every other week.
sentences.Hvordan går det? Er det travelt?: How's it going? Is it busy?
sentences.Ja. Jeg begynner på jobb klokka åtte og: Yes. I start work at eight o'clock and drop the children off at kindergarten and school before work. It's busy, but it's going fine. I usually get up early in the morning, because I like to have plenty of time. What do you do?
sentences.Jeg er lærer og underviser på norskkurs,: I'm a teacher and teach on a Norwegian course, and Marit is a teacher at a primary school. We live together.
sentences.Så hyggelig å høre. Nå må jeg skynde meg: How nice to hear. Now I have to hurry to work, because I'm short of time. Shall we have a coffee at the weekend?
sentences.Ja, gjerne! Jeg liker å gå på kafeen i S: Yes, I'd love to! I like going to the café in Storgata.
sentences.Fint! Det er en hyggelig kafé. Vi snakke: Great! It's a nice café. Talk to you at the weekend.
sentences.Jeg gleder meg. Ha det bra!: I'm looking forward to it. Bye!
Bjørnar has a lot to do.
He is divorced and has the children every other week.
He usually drops the children off before work.
It's busy, but it's going fine.
Håvard lives with his partner Marit.
sentences.Bjørnar og Håvard skal gå på kafé i helg: Bjørnar and Håvard are going to a café at the weekend.
